recipes.name: Sweet Polish Sausage
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds kielbasa sausage, cut into 1 inch pieces

steps.text: Place sausage in a large saucepan with enough water to cover; simmer over low heat for 1 hour. Drain. Transfer sausage to a 9x13-inch baking dish; set aside.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine onion, 2/3 cup water, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, and hot pepper sauce in same saucepan; bring to a boil, stirring. Pour over sausage.
Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Polish Sausage
raw_recipe.description: Cooked Polish kielbasa is baked in a Worcestershire-based sauce laced with lemon juice, brown sugar and hot pepper sauce.

review.reviewBody: We loved this! Instead of the stovetop method -I first boiled the sausage for about 10 minutes and then I through all of the ingredients together in my slow cooker and let the flavors meld together on low for 8 hours...YUMMY! Served it over rice with veggies on the side. So good we wish we had more sausage in the house to make it again tomorrow! Will do again and again...

Easy to make. I cooked it entirely in the crockpot. Onions and 3 chopped garlic cloves then the sliced sausage and poured the sauce on top. I did not cook the sauce. For the sauce I substituted pineapple juice for water, added a dash of soy sauce, a tablespoon of cornstarch.and topped it off with green onions. Cooked on high 3 hours. Served over steamed rice. Delicious

This is one of the best recipe and easy as well! I had this dish a whole meal by adding potatoes and making a few alterations. My SO couldn't get enough of this dish.
After I boiled the sausage for 20 minutes, I set it aside and added 5 chopped potatoes to the boil in the saucepan until they were only slightly tender. I drained and began the sauce, adding about a tablespoon of ketchup to the mix. Once that came to a boil, I added the potatoes to simmer for 10 minutes. I added the sausage to a deep baking dish, poured the potato/sauce mixture over and topped that a few seasonings: garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Then comes a layer of a half cup of shredded American cheese (the good deli stuff, don't go cheap on the cheese) and a sprinkle of fresh basil and parsley (mostly for added prettiness). Bake and watch it disappear!
On a final note, some homemade bread would be the perfect finish to this meal, as the sauce makes an irresistably great dip.

TL:DR Add potatoes, cheese, seasonings, and homemade bread.

I used UNCOOKED sausage, NOT smoked or precooked. I removed the casing. Loose meat made into balls works best. I slice up my sausage and let it cook in it's own juices for about 15 mins just to brown and cook half way. It'll finish cooking in the sauce. I omit the water but keep the drippings as the base to add all else to. I simmer covered on the stove, stirring occasionally, keeping it at a low boil, for another 30 min or until it thickens to my liking. Broccoli is a nice add in at the end. I served over mashed potatoes, white rice or wide egg noodles.
For a slightly less 'sweet' and 'richer' flavor, cut brown sugar to 1/4 cup and add 1/4 dark molasses. This is how I usually make it.
Just an old Southern way taught to me by my mom.

I took the advice of many people leaving reviews to use the slow cooker - I actually wished I had used MORE sausage and less onion -- it was SO good but too much onion (for my own liking). 

I ran the slow cooker after boiling the sausage on WARM for 25 minutes to let the ingredients really absorb the wet ingredients, followed by another 40 minutes on low, and finally finished on 40 minutes on high. It was tender, the onions had a little crunch left but nothing raw and the flavors were delicious.

We loved the flavor of this recipe. I followed DC in TX's suggestion and just put everything in the slow cooker after boiling the sausage for 10 minutes. An hour before eating, I mixed in about 2 tablespoons of cornstarch mixed with some water to thicken up the juice to serve it over rice. The only thing I would do different would be to saute the onions before adding them in; even after 8 hours, they were still crunchy, and we prefer a soft, cooked onion. Someone else mentioned pineapple juice and chunks...sounds like a nice idea too! Great versatile recipe.

Added 1 lg can chunk pineapple & sauce, omitted water & lemon juice. Reduced Worcestershire to 1/4 cup. Added heaping spoonful of cornstarch, and two dollops of ketchup. Heat sauce to marry flavors and cornstarch, then pour into square baking dish, over sausage, which was linked and boiled for about 15 mins. Cover w/foil & bake at 350 for 30 mins. Remove foil, stir, bake 30 more mins, stirring occasionally. Let cool 10 mins, stirring occasionally. Very good!

My husband said this is the best sausage he has ever had! I did cut the sugar in half and only boiled about 20 mins. Other than that, followed the rest of the recipe as written. Was amazing!! Thank you for a great twist on kielbasa!

I simmered the fresh Polish Sausage in beer for 1/2 hour or so and used chicken stock instead of water for flavor. Gonna make this again for sure but next time I'll need to thicken the sauce was too thin.

I make this at least once a month. I use andouille sausage and omit the hot sauce. I only boil for 15-20 minutes and use about 1 1/2 cups of the sausage water instead of plain water. I also saute the onions. We eat over rice. Everyone loves it!

I made this last night, and it was tasty. I had the precooked sausage also, so I only let it boil in the water for about 5 minutes. I also didn't have time to cook it in the oven for an hour and cooked at a higher temperature for 20 minutes. Next time I will try the crockpot method others mentioned, since it will likely give the meat more time to absorb the flavors. I also added a dash of cayenne pepper instead of hot pepper sauce since I didn't have any around. It gave it a nice kick but did overpower the other flavors a bit, so next time I may just leave that out or try chili pepper instead.
Great with noodles and cabbage. Will try with potatoes next time.
The only thing I changed was I replaced the onion with shallots. It was a hit at Easter. Would also make a great appetizer!

This is my go to meal!! It’s so easy! You can even use frozen kielbasa & it cooks beautifully. I omit the lemon juice & add a lil ketchup just to thicken it up a lil bit. Everyone that’s tried this asks for the recipe
My kids and I didn't like it. None of us liked the flavor. However, my husband loved it & I'll make it again for him.
Yummy! I had a 13oz. sausage and used 1/2 an onion. Made the sauce the same. Added Steam Fresh California Blend frozen vegetables the last 20 minutes. Put over Jasmine Rice.
I only had 1 pound of Polish Kielbasa but made the sauce with no changes. That was easy! It was extremely delicious! Don't pass this one up!
it was very good. I used pre-cooked Polish sausage/smoked sausage. it cut way back on the time required to prepare this recipe.
The dish itself it good and fairly simple to make.
I was torn between 2 stars and 3 stars. It was ok. I think too much trouble for the end results. I'll pass on this one.
